toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Applied the supplied diagnostic sequence at standard depth. Collected two items: X9 (transmitted setpoints and product-master change history) and X13 (controller telemetry and packing records). Together they test the setpoint-to-decay chain and rule out the main rivals (fungicide, Lower Serra fruit, carrier equipment, transit time).
output.brief:
The rejections trace to our own paperwork, not the carrier, the fungicide or Lower Serra fruit. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation system, the mandarin product record had been copied from avocado by the contractor, keeping a 7.0°C setting instead of our 4.0°C specification. The go-live review missed it.

All five containers sent at 7.0°C were rejected; all four sent at 4.0°C passed, including an earlier Meridane booking and Coastway loads using the new fungicide. Meridane's units held the setting we gave them. A load using the old fungicide still failed at 7.0°C, and transit time doesn't explain the split. Lower Serra fruit was in every container, passing ones included; its pallets decayed more inside rejected containers, but why isn't established.

Next: correct the product record; have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct; add a check of booking settings against specification; review the contractor's other records. Don't file the Meridane claim or suspend and withhold pay from Lower Serra. Hold any contractor deduction until the contract and our own sign-off are reviewed. Confidence: high on the main cause, moderate on Lower Serra.
